newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot electricity prices resume recent slump.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot electricity prices resume recent slump.

text.p: The spot bulk electricity market in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) began 1997 lower, resuming its recent slump linked to mild weather and falling cash prices in the natural gas market.
"The whole thing is that there is no demand," said an ERCOT trader.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Friday was talked in a $20.00-$22.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) range, down from $22.00-$23.00 Tuesday.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Friday's heavy load hours was assessed at $18.00-$19.00, down from Tuesday's $21.00-$22.00.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Friday were still valued at $9.00-$11.00.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Friday's light load hours held in a notional range of $8.50-$10.50.
With most major instate coal and nuclear power plants running, there has been little demand for natural gas for electricity production, market sources said.

Weather Services Corp's latest forecast showed Texas' temperatures would stay well-above normal through most of the weekend with day readings mostly in the 70 degrees Fahrenheit range and night readings in the 40s-60s, some 20 degrees above seasonal norms.

On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub gas futures were up 3.8 cents at $2.795 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu). Swing gas prices in south Texas fell about 10 cents to the $2.30 area from Tuesday's quotes.
Market participants said a cool weather system arriving late Sunday could increase short-term demand for gas and electricity next week.
"We should get a cold front Sunday. That may do something," said one hopeful ERCOT marketer.
The ERCOT forward market was very quiet today with July/August deliveries quoted at $25.00-$25.50, flat from Tuesday.
